answer: Operator liabilities pool. Each identity a wallet controls is tied to a shared insurance fund the operator must top up whenever any linked wallet fails verification; because the charge lands on the operator’s single account, cloning wallets yields no nectar for a cheater. A failed check triggers a gale of escrowed penalties drawn from that pool, sized so ten clones cost far more than ten honest registrations. Honest operators recover unused balances after a dune of clean audit cycles, while attackers forfeit the whole pool.
